question.text: The Ottomans conquered this capital city of the Byzantine Empire in May 1453. Give its name as of 1453, not its ancient name or its modern name, which was adopted in 1923.
question.answerHtml: Constantinople (do not accept or prompt on “Byzantium” or “Istanbul”)
question.clue: A road called the mese (MEH-say) ran through this city, which may have lost forty percent of its population in a plague in 542 CE. A gigantic cannon designed by Orban sufficed to break through this city's 60-foot-tall Theodosian Walls.

swap.text: The Byzantine Empire had several rulers with this common name; the first of whom usurped the throne from Michael III and founded the Macedonian dynasty, and the second was known as the Bulgar-slayer for his complete conquest of Bulgaria.
swap.clue: The Varangian Guard was expanded after a ruler of this name married his sister Anna to Vladimir I ("the first") of Kiev.

question.leadin: Procopius wrote a lively, if historically and logically dubious, account of this man's reign.
question.text: Name this Byzantine emperor and husband of Theodora who sought to reconquer the Western Roman Empire. He also constructed the Hagia Sophia.
question.clue: He expelled pagan teachers from the Academy in Athens.

swap.text: This legal code passed by Justinian is sometimes named after him, and is composed of three main parts with a minor fourth section. The Codex and Digest are two of those sections.
swap.clue: For centuries, scholars puzzled over how three million lines were reduced to 150,000 during this work's creation.

question.leadin: Procopius described this building as looking "as though it were suspended from heaven by [a] golden chain."
question.text: Name this former church constructed under Justinian that was later converted to a Mosque in 1453 during the Ottoman conquest of Constantinople.
question.answerHtml: Hagia Sophia [or Hagia Sophia Grand Mosque or Church of God’s Holy Wisdom]
question.clue: On its southwestern entrance of this building is a mosaic of two important emperors presenting models of this building and its city to the Virgin Mary.

swap.text: Khan Tervel of Bulgaria formed an alliance with the second emperor of this name in 704. The first Byzantine emperor with this name ordered the rebuilding of the Hagia Sophia (AI-uh SOF-yuh) and the recompilation of laws.
swap.clue: Before his first overthrow, he lost the Battle of Sebastopolis to the Umayyads, after which this ruler ordered the butchering of all the Slavs in Bithynia.

question.text: Justinian almost fled Constantinople during these riots that started after an angry crowd gathered at the Hippodrome.
question.clue: Participants in this event wanted to crown Hypatius, but were outmaneuvered by the eunuch Narses and slaughtered by Mundus.

swap.text: This general helped put down the Nika Riots with Mundus and Narses. This general led the campaigns against the Vandals and the Goths under Justinian the Great.
swap.clue: This general's campaigns informed Procopius's History of the Wars.

question.text: The Byzantine Empire went through periods characterized by this belief, the opposition to the use of religious images.
question.clue: The first attempt to apply this doctrine officially was met with resistance at the Chalke Gate, and it was condemned by the Second Council of Nicaea convoked by Irene.

swap.text: Funded by Venice, this crusade looted Constantinople in 1204 and gave up on reaching the Middle East.
swap.clue: Pope Innocent III excommunicated all of its participants when they attacked the Dalmatian capital in exchange for assistance from Enrico Dandolo, the doge of Venice.

question.leadin: Answer the following about the 1453 conquest of Constantinople by the Ottoman Empire.
question.text: The death of Constantine XI during the battle brought an end to the two hundred year rule of this final dynasty of Byzantine emperors.
question.clue: This dynasty's founder wedded his daughter into the noble family of Trebizond; that founder was Michael VIII. Its last ruler, Constantine XI, died in the Ottomans' siege of Constantinople.

swap.text: The Council of Clermont was ostensibly called to assist this embattled Byzantine emperor, who did not ask for a full-scale invasion of the Holy Land. Still, he took advantage of the Crusade to regain lost territory in Anatolia.
swap.clue: The insane monk Raiktor joined a force against this man that won the Battle of Dyrrhachium and Robert Guiscard.

question.text: This elite group of Norse fighters in the Byzantine army was formed when Basil the Bulgar-Slayer had his sister Anna married off to Vladimir the Great in exchange for their service.
question.clue: As punishment for replacing this group with loyal Scythians, Michael V ("the fifth") was castrated and blinded by Harald Hardrada.

swap.leadin: This dynasty's icon-hating was ended by its last ruler, Empress Irene of Athens.
swap.text: Name this dynasty of Leo the Khazar and Constantine VI. It came to power at the end of the Twenty Years' Anarchy and was supplanted by Nikephoros I.
swap.clue: The second ruler of this dynasty was nicknamed Copronymus after defecating in his baptismal font.

question.text: Before becoming emperor, Constantine ruled this despotate that encompassed much of the Peloponnese peninsula whose capital was Mystras.
question.clue: At that time, the entire Peloponnese was under the control of this Despotate, which had been established circa 1349 by Byzantine emperor John VI Cantacuzenus, and then taken over by the Palaeologus dynasty. It was ruled from a site near ancient Sparta.

swap.leadin: Name these dynasties or families that ran the Byzantine empire.
swap.text: Isaac I was the first emperor of this family, whose other members included Manuel I and a king of Cyprus named Isaac who fought Richard the Lionheart. Alexius I of this family let the First Crusade pass through.

question.text: This woman wrote admiringly of the manly traits of Empress Irene in her influential Byzantine history, The Alexiad.
question.clue: This woman may have been inspired by the material laid out by her husband Nikephoros Bryennios the Younger to write a chronicle of her father's rule named the Alexiad.

swap.leadin: This ruler recognized Stefan Nemanja ("NEH-mahn-yah") as the rightful zupan ("zhoo-pan") during an incredibly successful campaign through Serbia.
swap.text: Identify this expansionist Byzantine emperor whose reign was chronicled by his loyal historian John Cinnamus. He magnanimously forgave Raynald of Chatillon ("shah-tee-YON") for his Cyprian massacre in exchange for total fealty.
swap.clue: While this ruler's armies besieged the island of Corfu, the Venetians mocked this ruler by having an African slave impersonate him.

question.leadin: This clash took place near modern-day Konya, and the victory of the winning side is generally attributed to their ability to occupy the elevated position.
question.text: Identify this 1176 battle in which the forces of the Sultanate of Rum, led by Arslan II, inflicted an overwhelming defeat on the Byzantine army.

swap.text: This archbishop of Thessalonica is known for his eyewitness account of the city's sack by and the Odyssey . Norman forces in 1185 and for a set of commentaries on the Iliad
